sections.title: The digraph sh
paragraphs: The letters sh make the sound in (ship) /ʃɪp/, which means a large boat. This digraph makes one sound. A digraph means two letters that together write one sound. You hear this sound at the start, in the middle, or at the end of many everyday English words.

sections.title: How to say sh
paragraphs: Push your lips forward into a loose circle. Raise the front of your tongue just behind the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap. The sound is voiceless. Voiceless means the voice is off. Touch your throat to feel that it does not shake.

sections.title: Spelling of sh
paragraphs: The letters sh write this sound in regular spelling. You find it at the start of words like (ship) /ʃɪp/. You also find it at the end of words like (fish) /fɪʃ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not let your tongue tip touch your teeth. That mistake turns the sound into the s in sea. Pull your tongue back slightly, round your lips, and blow softly.
